body: This telling of the Coyote and Raven story is the version told at summer gatherings; there is a shorter winter version with a different ending that should be recorded separately with the elders' permission.
Some community members spell 'shéyu' as 'sheyu' without the accent in informal writing (e.g. text messages) — worth noting both forms in the community dictionary.
Second segment should be 'hu-tâ' not 'hu-tá' — the vowel here is mid tone in this speaker's dialect, ASR draft mis-marked it as high.
'waka loi' is more naturally translated as 'let's go' in this conversational context rather than a literal 'we go' — matches how it's used at the start of the recording.
ASR confidence is low on this whole session (tonal minimal pairs are hard for the mock/base model to distinguish) — needs full manual re-transcription by a linguist before any export.
